system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
On the grid, draw a line parallel to line L.

[Image: A grid with line L]

Figure, described in words:
A grid measuring 11 squares wide by 6 squares high. A straight line segment with arrowheads at both ends is labeled L near its upper-right end. The line follows the diagonals of grid squares at a 45-degree angle (slope of 1), extending from the grid intersection located 3 units from the left and 2 units from the bottom to the intersection located 6 units from the left and 5 units from the bottom.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw a straight line with arrowheads at both ends that also rises one square up for every one square across (a 45-degree slope, like L). For example, start at the grid intersection 0 squares from the left and 0 squares from the bottom... more precisely, start at the intersection 1 unit from the left and 0 units from the bottom and extend it diagonally up and to the right through (2,1), (3,2), (4,3), (5,4), (6,5), ending at the top edge of the grid (about 7 units from the left and 6 units from the bottom would be on the grid edge at (6,6)? ). Specifically: draw the line through the intersections (1,0), (2,1), (3,2), (4,3), (5,4), (6,5), so it is parallel to L and passes below and to the right of L, with the same slope of 1 (each step goes 1 square right and 1 square up).
